title: Rav Ika
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a great man in Abaye’s time. He married the sister of Rav Acha bar Yaakov, and she bore him Rav Acha. Hyman describes his son as so great that his father was called after his son, as in Avodah Zarah 65a: the father of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika used to pour wine for gentiles, taking it across a ferry, and they gave him jugs in payment; they came and told Abaye. In Ketubot 74a: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, the son of Rav Acha bar Yaakov’s sister.

In Bava Kamma 22a we find Rav Huna bar Manoach in Rav Ika’s name. There are Rav Idi son of Rav Ika, Yevamot 43a; Rav Huna son of Rav Ika, Pesachim 52b; Rav Chinena son of Rav Ika, Berakhot 25b; and Rav Shmuel son of Rav Ika, Avodah Zarah 69a.

notes.text: Saved Davidson English Avodah Zarah65a continues at65b: Ika received the jugs as payment. The remuneration reading is supported; no forced-labor gloss is introduced. Hyman’s inference from the son-based designation is attributed; nephew and father relations remain distinct.

The consulted Avodah Zarah 65a–65b confirms the jugs as remuneration. Its ensuing discussion explains the ferry crossing through an arrangement with the ferryman, rather than Ika personally transporting the forbidden wine; Hyman’s description above is compressed.
